origin: The kernel: Google's own figures show sizeable gains. The possible overstatement: "significant" and "substantial" rest on Google's self-selected benchmarks. "Half the original cost" is true only for the introductory per-token price, which expires at year end. Expected honest rating: 55 to 75.
author: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet
initial:

evidence_up.evidence_note: Real. Artificial Analysis on X, published 13 August 2026, 18:52 UTC, https://x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2087975627391717461 (fetched via fxtwitter), after the 17:05 UTC post.
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: later on 13 August 2026, the independent benchmarking firm Artificial Analysis published its evaluation of Gemini 3.7 Flash. It scored 56 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 4 points above Gemini 3.6 Flash, with the gain driven mainly by agentic evaluations: Terminal-Bench v2.1 rose 8 points and GDPval-AA v2 rose 103 Elo. It had the top score on AutomationBench-AA at 62.7%, ahead of Kimi K3 (53%) and GPT-5.6 Sol (51.2%), and the top score on AA-AnalystAgent at 60%, ahead of Claude Opus 5 (54%) and Claude Fable 5 (49%). At the discounted launch price it cost $0.40 per Intelligence Index task, 30% less than Gemini 3.6 Flash. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
